feed.title: Warren Buffett Was Never Just a Value Investor. Here’s the Real Secret to His Investing Success
feed.summary: A new research paper by Kai Wu reveals that Warren Buffett's investment success was not primarily driven by traditional value investing but by consistently buying high-quality businesses with strong intangible assets. His outperformance can largely be explained by factor exposures to intangible value and quality, rather than non-replicable stock-picking skill. The article suggests that individual investors can replicate Buffett's returns by systematically investing in companies with high intangible value and quality, a strategy applicable across various markets.

feed.title: Apple Spent Years Downplaying AI Chatbots. Now Siri Is Becoming One
feed.summary: Apple, which previously downplayed the utility of AI chatbots, is reportedly transforming its Siri assistant into a full-fledged, system-wide AI chatbot. This shift, according to Bloomberg, indicates Apple's concession that chatbots are a preferred interface for AI, moving away from its previous philosophy of subtly embedding AI within device features. The new Siri, code-named Campos, will be deeply integrated across Apple's operating systems and offer an experience more akin to ChatGPT.

feed.title: Apple urges court to stop Indian antitrust body from seeking financials: report

feed.title: Apple asks Indian court to stop antitrust body from seeking its financials
feed.summary: Apple is seeking a court order in India to prevent the country's antitrust watchdog, the Competition Commission of India (CCI), from requesting its global financial records. This move is part of a larger dispute where Apple challenges the validity of penalty rules and faces accusations of abusing its app store position. Apple fears a potential $38 billion fine if its global turnover is used for penalties, and argues that complying with financial requests now would undermine its legal challenge against India's current penalty regulations.

feed.title: Apple Pay Finally Launches in India After 10-Year Wait
feed.summary: After a decade of regulatory hurdles and banking complications, Apple Pay is finally entering India's digital payments market with an expected launch by the end of 2026. The delay was primarily due to India's data localization requirements and the incompatibility of Apple's biometric authentication methods (Face ID/Touch ID) with India's payment framework. Apple Pay's strategy will involve offering a premium payment experience to its growing user base in India, focusing on seamless ecosystem integration, enhanced security, and superior international transaction capabilities, rather than competing directly with existing UPI giants.

feed.title: Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) faces push for China supply-chain risk audit
feed.summary: The National Legal and Policy Center (NLPC) is urging Apple shareholders to vote for Proposal No. 5, requesting a "China Entanglement Audit." feed.title: Luck or Strategy? Why Boeing uses "7" in all its aircraft names
feed.summary: Boeing's iconic use of the number "7" in its aircraft names, such as the 707 and 787, originated from an internal numbering system in the 1950s where the 700 series was designated for commercial jet transports. The success of the Boeing 707 solidified this "7X7" pattern as a brand, making it instantly recognizable globally. While the company is nearing the end of available "7X7" combinations with only the 797 remaining for traditional designs, Boeing is exploring new naming conventions like 7A7-7Z7 or leveraging letters for variants to accommodate future revolutionary aircraft designs.

feed.title: Mutual Fund Managers Are Wrong More Than They’re Right
feed.summary: This article analyzes mutual fund managers' "hit rates" (percentage of holdings outperforming their benchmark index) and finds that most managers pick more losing stocks than winners. While higher hit rates generally correlate with less underperformance, the study concludes that portfolio construction, specifically the weighting of winning stocks, is more crucial than merely picking winners. Market returns are concentrated, meaning a few big winners drive most gains, and past hit rates are not reliable predictors of future success for mutual fund managers or individual investors.

feed.title: Everyone Expected Apple to Raise Prices on Its New Macs. What It Did Instead Was Much Smarter

feed.title: Apple unveils MacBook Neo, its most affordable model yet
feed.summary: Apple is preparing to launch its most affordable MacBook to date, the MacBook Neo, on March 11. Starting at around $600, this new model will feature a chip similar to the iPhone 16 Pro and will come with a smaller screen and less memory than other MacBooks. This strategic move follows a recent announcement regarding a lower-priced iPhone 17, aiming to attract budget-conscious consumers to Apple's laptop ecosystem.

feed.title: The MacBook Neo May Be Apple’s Most Consequential New Product in a Decade
feed.summary: Apple has announced the MacBook Neo, a new 13-inch laptop that significantly cuts the starting price of its Mac lineup, positioning it as a highly consequential product. This fanless device runs on an A18 Pro chip, marking the first time an A-series chip has been used in a Mac, making it an affordable and important re-entry into a market segment Apple has largely left untouched for over a decade. Starting at $599, or $499 for educational customers, it's one of Apple's most affordable computers in modern history.

feed.title: Logistics Costs Are Rewriting the Coffee Price Story in 2026
feed.summary: Despite a seemingly bearish global coffee market with futures prices falling and record harvests expected, actual delivered coffee costs are rising due to escalating logistics expenses. Geopolitical disruptions, particularly in the Red Sea, have led to increased container freight rates, longer shipping routes, and surging war-risk insurance premiums, creating a significant disconnect between futures market prices and the physical realities faced by roasters and importers. These factors are absorbing the benefits of lower futures prices, underscoring how logistics are reshaping the coffee supply chain and delaying the impact of projected surpluses.

feed.title: Apple holds talks with Intel, Samsung for US chipmaking, Bloomberg News reports

feed.title: Apple Extends Private Cloud Compute to Google Cloud on Nvidia Blackwell GPUs
feed.summary: Apple is expanding its Private Cloud Compute (PCC) platform to Google Cloud, marking the first time this privacy-focused infrastructure will operate outside Apple's own data centers. Apple retains full software control and transparency, publishing PCC binaries for inspection and extending its Security Bounty program to this new deployment.

feed.summary: Assurant's Q1 2026 Mobile Trade-In and Upgrade Industry Trends Report reveals that consumers received $1.63 billion in value through mobile trade-in programs, a 31% increase from 2025. This growth is driven by rising smartphone prices, the increasing demand for refurbished devices, and the role of protection plans in maintaining device condition for higher trade-in values. The report highlights how trade-ins help offset upgrade costs, expand access to more affordable smartphones, and support a circular mobile economy.

feed.title: UBS AG (AMUB) sells $29.48M autocallable GEARS due June 14, 2029
feed.summary: UBS AG has issued $29.48 million in Trigger Autocallable GEARS linked to a basket of 29 equities, maturing on June 14, 2029. These securities feature an autocall barrier at 100% of the initial basket level with a 22% call return rate. If not automatically called, the maturity payoff depends on basket performance with a 1.75 upside gearing and a downside threshold of 75%, exposing investors to potential principal loss.

feed.title: New BlackBerry tools let governments manage Macs without public cloud
feed.summary: BlackBerry (NYSE:BB) has announced significant enhancements to its Unified Endpoint Management (UEM) platform, addressing the growing demand for sovereign endpoint control, particularly among governments and regulated industries. The new capabilities, expected to roll out in summer 2026, include on-premises macOS management, post-quantum cryptography upgrades aligning with NIST standards for FIPS 140-3 accreditation, expanded multi-tenant support, and secure AI-assisted operations. These updates enable organizations to manage diverse device fleets without reliance on public cloud infrastructure, mitigating data residency and exfiltration risks.

feed.title: TSMC and Amkor sign 10-year deal to expand semiconductor packaging in Arizona
feed.summary: TSMC and Amkor Technology have entered a 10-year agreement to significantly expand advanced semiconductor packaging and test services in Peoria, Arizona, with a $7 billion facility expected to begin production by 2028. This partnership aims to create a more robust domestic chip supply chain in the US by co-locating packaging operations near TSMC's fabrication plant, leveraging technologies like InFO and CoWoS crucial for AI and high-performance computing. The initiative is strongly aligned with the CHIPS and Science Act, aiming to reduce reliance on overseas manufacturing and mitigate geopolitical risks for critical chip production.

feed.title: The Honda Passport TrailSport Continues Its Rugged Journey
feed.summary: The Honda Passport TrailSport is increasingly focused on off-roading, with Honda developing the new Trail Experience (HTX) app for the 2028 model. This app allows owners to record off-road data and video, sharing their adventures with others. Additionally, the 2028 Passport TrailSport is expected to receive further updates, including a tougher design and revised suspension for a higher ride height, aiming to compete with Toyota's TRD models.

feed.title: Qualcomm Inc Stock (QCOM) Opened Up by 3.03% on Jun 16: What Signal Does It Send?
feed.summary: Qualcomm Inc. (QCOM) stock rose 3.03% due to optimism surrounding a potential acquisition of AI chip startup Tenstorrent for $8-10 billion and increased analyst price targets ahead of its Investor Day. CEO Cristiano Amon’s vision for AI-enabled devices and a supportive macroeconomic environment further contributed to the stock's upward movement. However, the company faces risks such as acquisition integration challenges, geopolitical overhangs, potential multiple contraction, and continued margin compression in its licensing division due to Apple's transition away from Qualcomm modems.

feed.title: Garmin Forerunner 165 Music targets runners who want premium GPS without the flagship price
feed.summary: Garmin has released the Forerunner 165 Music, a new GPS running watch designed for everyday runners who desire premium features like a bright AMOLED display, reliable GPS, and on-wrist music at a more accessible price point. This model aims to bridge the gap between entry-level trackers and high-end flagship watches, offering features previously found in pricier models to a broader audience. It serves Garmin's strategy to retain its user base and appeal to serious amateur runners who are not looking for the most expensive devices.

feed.title: Apple Plans Camera AirPods Alongside Upgraded Foldable iPhone in 2027
feed.summary: Apple is reportedly planning to launch camera-equipped AirPods in late 2027, aiming to enter the AI device market. This release is expected alongside a next-generation foldable iPhone and a new iPhone model celebrating the product's 20th anniversary.
